assessment: The sand shrimp appears as a test species in the pesticide toxicology tables. The report considers environmental deposition, residues and susceptibility of marine species and does not evaluate fall frequency following shrimp intake.

assessment: The North Carolina estuarine environmental health cohort discussion includes shrimp fishing among local activities. The exposure pathway is contact with estuarine waters during such activities and the monitored endpoints concern suspected exposure-related illness.

Pandalus borealis is given as a predator of the copepod Calanus finmarchicus. The research profiles copepod gene expression and does not evaluate an edible-shrimp exposure or falls.
Brine and mysis shrimp were components of routine stickleback feed. The experimental contrast is maternal predator exposure and its association with embryonic gene expression.

Shrimp are environmental tissue samples included with seston, fish and porpoise in a PCB congener analysis. This is a contaminant occurrence assessment, without a boiled-shrimp intake or adult fall outcome.

assessment: Shrimp appears in the name of a pathogen’s host in a cellular virology review. The observations concern early host responses and provide no food preparation or fall-frequency comparison.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6096556/ (PCB contaminants in fish and seafood, northern Norway comparison)
assessment: Shrimp and halibut fillet are examples from a survey of contaminants in seafood. The paper discusses dietary contaminant burden and environmental monitoring without analyzing human falls.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6788496/ (Animal rearing and feeding, discussion of substrate)
assessment: Brine shrimp were routine feed for juvenile lake sturgeon. The authors mention feed falling between substrate particles while discussing fish foraging efficiency and metabolic development.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7064764/ (Aiptasia cultures, feeding methods and cell cycle measurements)
assessment: Brine shrimp nauplii were feed for anemones in an experiment on symbiosis, feeding and symbiont cell-cycle distribution. The study population has no clinical fall-frequency outcome.

Small copepods and shrimp are prey mentioned in observations of the pipefish around protective algae. The report concerns taxonomy and fish ecology rather than human dietary intake or falls.

assessment: The neurodegeneration commentary discusses differential toxicity of BMAA and an analog in brine shrimp. Acute toxicity in the test organism cannot identify an effect of dietary boiled shrimp on falls.

assessment: The review describes shrimp aquaculture as a potential pollution source and discusses pollutant concentrations in edible giant freshwater prawns. The health discussion uses estimated contaminant risk without conducting a falls comparison.
Shrimp alkaline phosphatase is listed as a laboratory reagent for cleaning up products for sequencing. The biological study concerns zoantharian symbionts during a stress event.

Mantis and snapping shrimp are reference examples for rapid strike mechanics in a spider biomechanics paper. Outcomes are movements of the spiders’ jaws and do not concern dietary exposure or patient falls.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9465362/ (Biogenic amines in seafood preservation, intervention table)
assessment: Shrimp and shrimp paste are preservation substrates in comparisons of tea polyphenols and other treatments. The measured changes are food concentrations of biogenic amines during storage.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9521177/ (Edible coating treatment table and oxidative stability section)
assessment: White shrimp is listed among foods coated with clove essential oil or related preparations to preserve quality. The reported comparisons concern storage oxidation or spoilage and do not observe clinical falls.

Shrimp shells and exoskeletons appear as chitin sources. Pink-shrimp chitin adsorption of lead from aqueous solution is a tested material property rather than a boiled-shrimp intervention in patients.

assessment: The article compares film formulations to track refrigerated rainbow trout freshness and cites separate work on preserving refrigerated shrimp. No human feeding or fall assessment was conducted.

assessment: Shrimp and mantis shrimp are species in aquatic contaminant biomonitoring and trophic-transfer examples. Consumption risk is modeled from contaminant concentrations without a falls endpoint.
Shrimp and crab shells are sources of isolated chitosan used in drug carrier formulations, including rodent testing. This is a pharmaceutical material, with no boiled-food or patient falls contrast.

The killifish eat live brine shrimp under the general husbandry schedule. Age-related tissue transcriptomes and biomarkers are the outcomes, without an intervention contrasting shrimp and adult falls.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13010698/ (Food and water section, aquatic dietary microplastics pathway)
assessment: Shrimp and small fish eaten whole are discussed as potentially concentrated sources of incidental microplastic exposure. The general aging review gives no original boiled-shrimp or fall-frequency measure.
Some whalefish specimens were collected as bycatch from a Sakura shrimp fishery. Shrimp is part of the specimen provenance and the study outcomes concern fish taxonomy.
Brine shrimp was the standard zebrafish feed. The tested intervention is trihexyphenidyl after chronic unpredictable stress and the outcomes concern zebrafish depression-like behaviour and signaling.
Dried or fresh shrimp is listed as a flavoring or filling in ethnobotanical documentation of zongzi recipes. The original records capture recipe use and cultural practices without comparing falls.
Brine shrimp nauplii are used as a cytotoxicity model in a formulation study described in the review. This is preclinical pharmaceutical testing without a dietary shrimp exposure or a falls outcome.

assessment: Shrimp-shell chitosan is a commercial polymer ingredient of selenium and Mucuna nanoconjugates. The test formulation and experimental model endpoints do not establish an effect of eating boiled shrimp on patient falls.
